themes.consensus_view: Banks agree AI spending keeps climbing, with Alphabet lifting its 2026 capital-spending plan to $200bn, but they split on whether that spending can keep getting funded, with JPMorgan seeing demand outrun supply while Bank of America says bond investors have stopped paying for it.

facts_agreed.claim: Several desks are treating the return on AI capital spending as an open question rather than a settled one.
The AI capital-spending cycle is an active, broadly tracked subject across desks this window.

facts_contested.claim: Whether AI capital spending can keep being financed, or whether funding conditions are already breaking it
facts_contested.for_evidence: demand continues to outpace supply across both its product and foundry businesses
facts_contested.against_evidence: bondholders are no longer funding the AI party

themes.consensus_view: Five desks are all watching how the big cloud companies are paying for their AI buildout — borrowing costs, bond issuance, and whether spending turns into cash — but none has yet said whether their bonds or their stock is the better place to be.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks are tracking how hyperscalers fund their AI spending, flagging debt issuance, funding durability, and credit spreads as live topics this window without taking a side.
Goldman ties the outlook for hyperscaler bonds to whether forecasts for the cash these companies generate start improving.
evidence_quotes: The path ahead for credit likely hinges on some improvement in forward estimates of free cash flow generation.

themes.consensus_view: Four desks flag the US midterms as a live macro risk this window, mostly around split-government gridlock and its hit to government spending, but none has staked out a directional call on stocks yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks are flagging the US midterm elections as an upcoming source of policy uncertainty, with split-government gridlock and reduced government spending the specific worries.
Deutsche Bank points to the historical pattern that the S&P 500 has recovered in the nine months after every one of the last 20 midterm elections.
evidence_quotes: by nine months later it has never been lower in any of the 20 midterm cycles

themes.consensus_view: Three of the four desks covering chips say the sell-off is not finished yet, blaming crowded trades being unwound and new Chinese memory-chip supply rather than worse earnings, while only JPMorgan still backs the bull case, so the sector's direction is genuinely unresolved.

facts_agreed.claim: The semiconductor complex is in a broad, forced repricing rather than a normal pullback, with selling pressure showing up across desks.
evidence_quotes: the magnitude of the recent sell-off appears more reflective of positioning, deleveraging and behavioral finance
concerns about the cyclical nature of other AI components are getting repriced
that sort of trade in the face of a well publicized 'backstop' suggests we still have a ways to go

facts_contested.claim: whether the semiconductor drawdown is a buyable dip or has further downside to run
facts_contested.for_evidence: We agree with the Bull Case.
facts_contested.against_evidence: that sort of trade in the face of a well publicized 'backstop' suggests we still have a ways to go

facts_contested.claim: whether the sell-off reflects deteriorating fundamentals or just positioning unwind
facts_contested.for_evidence: the magnitude of the recent sell-off appears more reflective of positioning, deleveraging and behavioral finance
facts_contested.against_evidence: concerns about the cyclical nature of other AI components are getting repriced

themes.consensus_view: Both desks read the current violent rotation between stocks as crowded traders unwinding the same positions at once rather than as a change in the underlying business fundamentals.

facts_agreed.claim: The recent rotation is being driven by traders exiting crowded positions, not by new fundamental news, and that unwind is now visibly underway.
evidence_quotes: prevailing view across investors remains that this is still primarily a positioning and momentum-driven rotation
the dispersion unwind we have been watching for is no longer hypothetical

themes.consensus_view: Three desks are tracking China's push to build its own DUV chipmaking machines (the tools that print circuits onto silicon) and what that means for memory-chip supply, but none has committed to a directional call yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks flag China's domestic DUV lithography tool production and its knock-on effect on Chinese memory-chip supply as a live topic this window.

themes.consensus_view: Three banks keep flagging Iran and the Strait of Hormuz shipping chokepoint as a live risk to oil supply, but none of them has committed to a call on which way oil actually goes.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks treat the Strait of Hormuz as an active geopolitical risk to oil supply in this window.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz supply disruption risk

facts_agreed.claim: Two banks flag the Iran conflict itself as a driver of energy and oil prices.
evidence_quotes: War in Iran impact on oil prices
